chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or intellectual benefit of trade in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) asserts that trade increases intellect, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that practical engagement in the world cultivates wisdom and discernment. This hadith underscores the dignity of commerce not merely as an economic necessity but as a means of spiritual and intellectual refinement, aligning with the principle that worldly activities, when conducted with integrity, serve as a path to higher understanding.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from the one who narrated it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from those who narrated to him who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Doing business increases one’s power of reason.’”
